statements.t: All statements, other than statements of historical fact included in this Quarterly Report including, without limitation, statements in this “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” regarding the Company’s financial position, business strategy, plans and objectives of management for future operations, including the expected completion of the acquisitions of…
We are a fintech-driven business-to-business platform that expects to power innovation in fintech, investing, underwriting and trading.

Our target client base for our prime banking and prime brokerage services includes financial services firms, generally with annual revenues up to $1 billion, including brokerage firms, hedge funds, pension plans, and family offices that are not adequately served by today’s larger correspondent clearing firms and banks.

(formerly Wilson-Davis & Co) (“AtlasClearing”), a correspondent clearing company, and the anticipated acquisition of Commercial Bancorp, we provide specialized clearing and banking services to financial services firms, with an emphasis on global markets currently underserviced by larger vendors.

The Company has made an earnest money deposit payment in the amount of $100,000 to Commercial Bancorp, which deposit will be applied to the cash portion of the consideration payable at the CB Closing or, if the CB Closing does not occur under certain circumstances, retained by Commercial Bancorp.
If the Company fails to timely deliver the shares of common stock issuable upon exercise of the 2025 Warrants, the Company will be subject to liquidated damages.
The Company will be subject to liquidated damages if it fails to meet certain conditions set forth in the Registration Rights Agreement.
In addition, additional cash commitments are expected for $2.44 million due at the Ark closing, and the Company has a $2.5 million seller note maturing in January 2027.

While management does not anticipate requiring capital beyond baseline operational expectations, these funding mechanisms are available, and management believes them to be sufficient to absorb any liquidity shortfalls during the assessment period.

Based on the available capital resources and management’s operational and financial mitigation plans, management expects to have sufficient liquidity to satisfy its obligations as they become due for at least twelve months following the date these condensed consolidated financial statements are issued.
